options.B: To help couples make informed reproductive choices
options.C: To provide immediate blood transfusions to carriers
options.D: To eliminate all infectious diseases in the community

explanation: Pre-marital screening and genetic counseling allow couples to understand their carrier status and make informed decisions regarding family planning to reduce the birth of children with sickle cell disease. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h7)

question: What primary necessity drove the earliest experiments in tele-health during the mid-20th century?

options.A: The desire to replace all bedside nurses with computers
options.B: The need to reach individuals in isolated geographic locations
options.C: Government mandates to eliminate paper medical records
options.D: Commercial demands for video gaming technology

explanation: Early tele-health emerged out of necessity to provide care to people in isolated places like rural areas, military settings, and space programs. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which type of exercise involves muscle contraction without changing the length of the muscle or moving the joint?

options.A: Isotonic exercise
options.B: Isometric exercise
options.C: Aerobic exercise
options.D: Isokinetic exercise

explanation: Isometric exercises involve muscle contraction without joint movement, making them useful for immobilized limbs. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h5)

question: How is postpartum hemorrhage actively prevented during the third stage of labor in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Through the active management of the third stage using uterotonics like oxytocin
options.B: By withholding all fluids from the mother
options.C: By delaying cord clamping indefinitely without medication
options.D: By performing immediate hysterectomy on all clients

explanation: Active management of the third stage of labor involves using uterotonics such as oxytocin to prevent postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h4)

question: Why is the chemical name of a drug rarely used in routine clinical nursing practice?

options.A: It is too expensive to print
options.B: It only identifies the manufacturer
options.C: It uses complex scientific terminology describing molecular structure
options.D: It changes with every country's pharmacopoeia

explanation: Chemical names describe complex atomic and molecular structures, making them impractical for everyday clinical communication. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h1)
